title: Weekday slice deploy cheatpad + release gazette (Dec 2026) - WIP
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact runbook for a half-day "weekday slice" deploy pattern: small traffic slices, staged regional ramp, and an internal 'Release Gazette' (one-paragraph summary) we publish to stakeholders after the window. The goal is to ship a low-risk infra+runtime change (KV cache pre-warming and a batching tweak) with minimal customer impact and good observability for fast rollback if required.

Scope / When to use:
- Low-risk infra or runtime config changes (non-model changes)
- No schema migrations or client-facing API changes
- Deploy windows during quiet business hours on weekdays (local region slack windows)

High-level timeline (example half-day window):
- T-minus 72h: owners assigned, smoke test deck prepared, e2e tickets linked
- T-minus 24h: preflight run in staging with 2x production traffic replay, escalation contacts confirmed
- D-day 09:00 - 09:30: preflight verification in canary cluster, dry-run smoke tests
- D-day 09:30 - 10:30: 1% traffic slice -> verify 30m
- D-day 10:30 - 11:30: 5% traffic slice -> verify 30m
- D-day 11:30 - 12:30: 20% traffic slice -> verify 30m
- D-day 12:30 - 13:00: full ramp (if all green) or stop/rollback
- D+0 14:00: Release Gazette (internal summary + open action items)

Preflight checklist (must be green before D-day):
- [ ] Staging run completed with traffic replay (errors <= baseline + 0.5%)
- [ ] Smoke test deck (repo: /tests/smoke/weekday-slice) updated and reviewed
- [ ] Canary infra snapshot saved and backup tag created
- [ ] Observability dashboards pinned: p95 latency, 99th token latency, errors, token cost, CPU/GPU utilization, kv_cache_hit_rate
- [ ] Rollback playbook published and owners oncall-aware
- [ ] Runbook channel created in Slack: #deploy-weekday-slice-<date> with invites to SRE, serving-runtime, release-engineering, devowner
- [ ] Customer-facing comms pre-drafted (if customer-impact possible)

Deploy steps (operator guide):
1) Create canary deployment with 1% traffic routing rule (feature-flag + routing tag).
2) Start KV-cache pre-warm job against canary nodes (script: infra/scripts/kv-warmup.sh) — record run output.
3) Apply batching config tweak via feature flag gate.
4) Run smoke tests against canary endpoints: basic generation, chat flow happy path, long-sequence stress (sample payloads in tests/smoke).
5) Monitor live metrics during verification window. Document p95 and error baselines.
6) If green, bump to 5% slice: update routing rules, re-run pre-warm if new nodes added.
7) Repeat verification and logs sampling.
8) If green, bump to 20%, then to full ramp per timeline.

Verification checks (automatic + manual):
- Automated checks (alerts should be muted to avoid noise during ramp but recorded):
  - error_rate_5m > baseline * 1.3 -> alert to channel and pause ramp
  - p95_latency_60s > baseline + 150ms -> page SRE and consider rollback
  - token_cost_per_minute spike > 25% -> pause and investigate batching regressions
  - kv_cache_hit_rate drops > 15% -> suspect cache invalidation bug
- Manual sanity checks (ops):
  - Review sample request/response traces for increased decoding truncation or malformed outputs
  - Check model routing fallbacks happened (if any) and counts
  - Confirm autoscaler not thrashing (no repeated pod churn > 3 instances in 10m)

Rollback matrix (simple rules):
- Trigger: error_rate > baseline * 1.3 for > 5m -> rollback to previous config tag (revert feature flag -> immediate 100% rollback via routing rule)
- Trigger: p95 > baseline + 200ms for > 5m -> pause ramp, triage; if unresolved in 20m -> rollback
- Trigger: customer-impacting telemetry (uptick in 500s or chat truncations customer reports) -> immediate rollback and page escalation
- Rollback steps: run rollback script infra/scripts/rollback-to-tag.sh <tag>, confirm routing rule reverted, monitor for stabilization 10m, then file incident note

Observability snippets to capture during window (operators):
- Dashboard snapshot export (png) at start and after each slice bump
- Top 10 stack traces by service (if errors)
- Sample 30 request traces for each verification window with timing breakdown (queue, model, decode)

Communication templates (short):
- Slack status updates (every 30m during active ramp):
  - "09:30 | Slice 1% applied. Smoke tests: pass. p95 120ms (+10ms). Errors 0.02% (baseline 0.018%). Monitoring."
- Pager-style escalation message (if paging):
  - "PAGING: Weekday Slice Deploy 12/06 — p95 exceeded threshold (380ms). Rolling back to tag v2026.11. Please join #deploy-weekday-slice-2026-12-06"

Release Gazette (post-deploy one-paragraph summary to send at D+0 + delivered to #prod-notify):
- Title: "Release Gazette: Weekday Slice - KV warmup + batching tweak (2026-12-06)"
- Body sample: "We rolled out a small runtime change to improve KV warming and batching heuristics across serving clusters. Deployment used a staged weekday-slice pattern (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> full) and completed at 12:40 UTC. No customer-facing errors observed; p95 latency improved by ~12ms on average in canary and held steady in prod. Action items: (1) follow-up load-run in staging to validate warmup with larger sequence distributions, (2) a small telem dashboard consolidation PR. Owners: Maya Patel (release), Ethan Brooks (SRE)."

Post-deploy notes / what to capture for the postmortem (if anything goes wrong):
- Timeline of every slice bump with absolute metric snapshots
- All slack messages and candidate traces
- Who ran which step (operator names) and their local clocks
- Attach dashboard snapshots and smoke test logs

Open questions / TODOs (work items before next weekday-slice):
- Can we add an automated preflight that runs the kv pre-warm job in staging and measures effective hit-rate uplift? (TODO: infra/automation)
- Should we add an intermediate 10% slice for latency-sensitive services? cost/ops tradeoff analysis needed.
- Confirm legal/customer comms threshold: at what customers do we send a brief pre-notice for infra-only changes? (marketing & customer-success ask)

Notes to self / troubleshooting tips:
- If kv_cache_hit_rate drops unexpectedly after ramp, check for a config mismatch in prefix hashing (common cause) — quick fix: revert to prior hash seed in config-store.
- If token costs spike, lower batch size via feature flag and re-evaluate.

Appendix: quick commands (operator cheatsheet)
- Create 1% slice: infra/ctl route set --service serving --tag canary-2026-12-06 --percent 1
- Revert to tag: infra/ctl route set --service serving --tag stable --percent 100
- Trigger kv warmup: infra/scripts/kv-warmup.sh --cluster canary-2026-12-06 --samples 10000 > /tmp/kvwarm.out

End of draft.

-- Maya

(Notes: keep this slim; this doc is intentionally lightweight — canonical playbooks and deep runbooks still live in the Release Runbook library. This is a field-ready cheatpad + rapid summary template we can use for small pre-approved weekday windows.)
